chunks: And by his chain, he said, Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said:
There are three signs for the show-off: He is active when he sees the people, and he is lazy when he is alone, and he loves to be praised in the entirety of his affairs.

key_terms.لِلْمُرَائِي: for the show-off (one who performs deeds for public display)

ai.seo_question: What are the three signs of showing off (riya) according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) identifies three key characteristics of a person who practices riya (showing off): increased energy in the presence of others, laziness when alone, and a desire for praise in all matters. This hadith highlights the contrast between public performance and private neglect as indicators of insincerity. In Shia scholarship, this triad is often viewed as a diagnostic tool for spiritual authenticity, linking the external behavior of 'activity' and 'praise-seeking' to the internal state of the heart, which must be purified from the love of creation's approval to achieve true ikhlas (sincerity).

en.hubeali:
And by his chain, 
‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘
There are three signs for the show-off – He is active when he sees the people (around him), and he is lazy when he is alone, and he loves to be praised in the entirety of his affairs’.
en.sarwar: 8. He (Ali ibn Ibrahim) has narrated through his chain of narrators the following: “Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) has said, ‘
A showoff has three signs: he is very active when people are present, very lazy when he is alone and he loves to be praised in all matters.’”
